title: Disorderly Conduct
description: Willfully engaging in unreasonable or disruptive conduct that materially interferes with public peace, safety, or ordinary use of a public place.

subsections.text: Fighting, challenging another person to fight, or creating a public disturbance.
Using threatening or persistently disruptive conduct after a lawful warning.
Blocking a public entrance, roadway, sidewalk, or emergency access without lawful purpose.

title: Public Intoxication
description: Being under the influence in a public place while unable to safely care for oneself or creating a public safety concern.

subsections.text: Being unable to safely stand, walk, communicate, or care for oneself because of intoxication.
Creating a hazard to pedestrians, motorists, or emergency personnel while intoxicated.
Refusing reasonable assistance while continuing conduct that creates an immediate safety risk.

title: Trespassing
description: Knowingly entering or remaining on private or restricted property after notice that entry is prohibited or after a lawful order to leave.

subsections.text: Entering property marked or posted against unauthorized entry.
Remaining after the owner, authorized agent, or peace officer orders the person to leave.
Entering a restricted government area without authorization.

title: Harassment
description: Repeated unwanted conduct directed at a person that serves no legitimate purpose and would cause a reasonable person substantial distress or fear.

subsections.text: Repeated unwanted contact, messages, or following after being told to stop.
Using threats or intimidation to deliberately cause substantial emotional distress.
Targeting an on-duty government or emergency worker.

title: Criminal Threats
description: Willfully communicating a credible threat of death or serious bodily injury under circumstances causing reasonable fear the threat will be carried out.

subsections.text: Threatening a person with death or serious bodily injury.
Threatening a family member, witness, or protected person to influence conduct.
Making a threat while displaying a weapon or apparent means of immediate execution.

title: Unlawful Assembly
description: Participating in a gathering that knowingly becomes violent, destructive, or substantially obstructive after a lawful dispersal order.

subsections.text: Remaining with a violent or destructive assembly after a lawful dispersal order.
Supplying weapons or tools for unlawful destruction.
Blocking emergency access or evacuation routes as part of the assembly.

title: Obstruction of Emergency Operations
description: Knowingly interfering with an active police, fire, EMS, rescue, or other emergency operation in a manner creating substantial risk.

subsections.text: Entering or remaining inside an established emergency perimeter without authorization.
Moving barriers, cones, vehicles, or equipment protecting an emergency scene.
Interfering with emergency personnel performing a rescue or life-safety function.

title: Simple Assault
description: Attempting or threatening unlawful physical force against another person while creating reasonable fear of imminent harmful contact.

subsections.text: Attempting to strike, kick, shove, or otherwise unlawfully apply force.
Threatening immediate physical harm while possessing apparent ability to carry it out.
Using force in a manner that does not cause serious bodily injury.

title: Battery
description: Willfully and unlawfully applying physical force or violence to another person without legal justification.

subsections.text: Unlawfully striking, kicking, pushing, grabbing, or otherwise applying force.
Applying force after the victim has withdrawn or is attempting to disengage.
Battery committed during another offense may be charged separately when independently established.

title: Aggravated Battery
description: Willfully inflicting significant bodily injury or using a dangerous instrument in an unlawful battery.

subsections.text: Causing serious bodily injury requiring substantial medical treatment.
Using a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument during the battery.
Knowingly targeting a restrained, unconscious, or defenseless person.

title: Kidnapping
description: Unlawfully moving, confining, or holding another person against that person's will by force, threat, deception, or intimidation.

subsections.text: Moving a person from one location to another without lawful consent.
Holding a person in a vehicle, building, room, or other place against their will.
Demanding property, information, or action as a condition of release.

title: False Imprisonment
description: Knowingly and unlawfully restricting another person's freedom of movement without the additional elements required for kidnapping.

subsections.text: Blocking a person's only reasonable means of exit.
Using force, threats, or restraints to prevent lawful departure.
Maintaining unlawful confinement after the person clearly requests release.

title: Child Endangerment
description: Knowingly placing a minor in circumstances creating a substantial and unreasonable risk of serious injury or death.

subsections.text: Leaving a child in a dangerous environment without adequate supervision.
Knowingly exposing a child to violent criminal activity or dangerous contraband.
Using a child to facilitate, conceal, or participate in a criminal offense.

title: Petty Theft
description: Unlawfully taking property belonging to another with intent to permanently deprive the owner when the property is below the felony threshold.

subsections.text: Taking merchandise or personal property without consent.
Concealing merchandise with intent to leave a business without payment.
Taking property from a vehicle or unattended location without authorization.

title: Grand Theft
description: Unlawfully taking property valued at or above $2,500, or specially protected property designated by the code.

subsections.text: Taking property valued at or above $2,500.
Taking a firearm, official emergency equipment, or specially protected property.
Taking property by stealth, deception, or concealment with felony intent.

title: Robbery
description: Taking personal property from a person or immediate presence through force, intimidation, or a credible threat of force.

subsections.text: Taking property directly from a person through physical force.
Taking property by threatening immediate physical harm.
Using restraints or coordinated intimidation to obtain property.

title: Armed Robbery
description: Robbery committed while armed with or displaying a firearm, dangerous weapon, or realistic object perceived as capable of serious injury.

subsections.text: Displaying a firearm during the commission of a robbery.
Using a knife, blunt weapon, or other dangerous instrument.
Using an imitation firearm or realistic weapon replica to facilitate the robbery.

title: Burglary
description: Entering a building, vehicle, vessel, or secured area without authorization with intent to commit theft or another felony.

subsections.text: Unlawfully entering a residence with criminal intent.
Unlawfully entering a commercial or government structure with criminal intent.
Unlawfully entering a secured vehicle, vessel, or storage area with criminal intent.

title: Motor Vehicle Theft
description: Taking, operating, or retaining a motor vehicle without the owner's consent and with intent to deprive the owner of possession.

subsections.text: Taking a vehicle without the owner's permission.
Operating a vehicle known to be stolen.
Possessing, concealing, or transferring a stolen vehicle or major component.

title: Receiving Stolen Property
description: Knowingly receiving, purchasing, possessing, concealing, or transferring property that the person knows or reasonably should know is stolen.

subsections.text: Possessing property with circumstances showing it was stolen.
Buying or accepting property at a clearly unreasonable price under suspicious circumstances.
Selling or transferring property while knowing it was stolen.

title: Vandalism
description: Willfully damaging, defacing, destroying, or materially altering property belonging to another without authorization.

subsections.text: Damaging public or private property.
Spraying, marking, painting, or defacing a structure without permission.
Damaging emergency, transportation, or government property is aggravating.

title: Resisting Arrest
description: Knowingly using physical resistance or active evasion to prevent a peace officer from lawfully taking the person into custody.

subsections.text: Pulling away, fighting, or physically preventing handcuffing after lawful arrest.
Running from an officer after being clearly ordered to stop under lawful arrest authority.
Using a vehicle or another person to actively prevent the arrest.

title: Obstruction of Justice
description: Knowingly interfering with a lawful investigation, proceeding, arrest, evidence process, or judicial function.

subsections.text: Destroying, hiding, altering, or fabricating evidence.
Knowingly misleading investigators through material false information.
Using force, threats, or intimidation to interfere with a witness or proceeding.

title: Failure to Identify
description: Refusing, after lawful detention based on reasonable suspicion or probable cause, to provide legally required identifying information.

subsections.text: Refusing to provide name when lawfully required during a qualifying detention.
Providing intentionally false identifying information.
Using another person's identifying information to defeat lawful identification.

title: Impersonating a Peace Officer
description: Falsely representing oneself as a peace officer or exercising apparent police authority without lawful appointment or authorization.

subsections.text: Claiming to be a sworn peace officer without lawful authority.
Displaying false credentials, badges, or markings to create police authority.
Using false police authority to detain, search, seize property, or obtain a benefit.

title: Witness Tampering
description: Knowingly attempting to influence, intimidate, threaten, corrupt, or prevent a witness from providing truthful information.

subsections.text: Threatening or intimidating a witness.
Offering money, property, or another benefit for false testimony or silence.
Retaliating against a witness because of participation in an investigation.

title: Unlawful Possession of a Firearm
description: Possessing a firearm while legally prohibited from possession or without a required state authorization.

subsections.text: Possessing a firearm while prohibited by a court order or qualifying conviction.
Possessing an unlawfully transferred firearm when registration is required.
Knowingly possessing a firearm for an unlawful purpose.

title: Carrying a Concealed Weapon
description: Carrying a concealed deadly weapon in a manner prohibited by licensing or location restrictions.

subsections.text: Concealing a handgun without a required permit or authorization.
Carrying a concealed weapon into a prohibited government or secure facility.
Failing to comply with a lawful weapon inspection during a qualifying stop.

title: Brandishing a Weapon
description: Displaying or handling a weapon in a threatening manner without lawful necessity, causing reasonable fear of unlawful violence.

subsections.text: Displaying a firearm during a confrontation without lawful defensive necessity.
Pointing a firearm or weapon at another person without legal justification.
Displaying a weapon to intimidate, threaten, or compel another person.

title: Unlawful Discharge of a Firearm
description: Discharging a firearm in a public place or toward another person, structure, vehicle, or occupied area without lawful justification.

subsections.text: Discharging a firearm in a public place without lawful justification.
Discharging toward an occupied building, vehicle, or area.
Discharging from or across a public roadway in a manner creating a safety risk.

title: Possession of a Controlled Substance
description: Knowingly possessing a controlled substance without a valid prescription, authorization, or other lawful basis.

subsections.text: Possessing a controlled substance for personal use.
Possessing quantities or packaging indicating possible distribution intent.
Possession in a restricted government facility is an aggravating circumstance.

title: Possession of Drug Paraphernalia
description: Knowingly possessing equipment primarily intended or adapted for unlawfully using, packaging, processing, or distributing controlled substances.

subsections.text: Possessing pipes, syringes, scales, baggies, or similar equipment with unlawful drug-use indicators.
Possessing equipment modified specifically for controlled-substance processing.
Possession with controlled substances may support separate charges when independently established.

title: Possession with Intent to Distribute
description: Possessing a controlled substance under circumstances demonstrating an intent to sell, transfer, or distribute it unlawfully.

subsections.text: Possessing quantities, packaging, ledgers, scales, or communications consistent with distribution.
Possessing individually packaged units prepared for sale.
Arranging an unlawful sale or transfer while possessing the controlled substance.

title: Manufacture of a Controlled Substance
description: Knowingly producing, processing, synthesizing, cultivating, or preparing a controlled substance without lawful authorization.

subsections.text: Operating a location or equipment used to manufacture controlled substances.
Possessing precursor materials with active manufacturing equipment and criminal intent.
Packaging or processing an unlawfully manufactured substance for distribution.

title: Drug Trafficking
description: Knowingly transporting, importing, exporting, or coordinating distribution of controlled substances on a commercial or organized scale.

subsections.text: Transporting controlled substances for another person in exchange for compensation.
Coordinating large-scale movement of controlled substances.
Using a vehicle, vessel, aircraft, or organized network to facilitate trafficking.

title: Speeding
description: Operating a motor vehicle above the posted or otherwise lawful speed limit where the conduct is not independently reckless.

subsections.text: Exceeding the posted limit by 1 to 15 MPH.
Exceeding the posted limit by 16 to 30 MPH.
Exceeding the posted limit by more than 30 MPH is an aggravating traffic violation.

title: Reckless Driving
description: Driving with willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property.

subsections.text: Driving at a speed or in a manner creating a substantial risk of collision.
Unsafe passing, lane use, or maneuvering with conscious disregard for safety.
Street racing or competitive driving on a public roadway.

title: Driving Under the Influence
description: Operating or being in actual physical control of a motor vehicle while impaired by alcohol, drugs, or a combination of substances.

subsections.text: Operating while alcohol impairment materially reduces safe driving ability.
Operating while impaired by a controlled substance or medication.
Operating with a prohibited blood or breath alcohol concentration established by approved testing.

title: Hit and Run
description: Leaving the scene of a collision without stopping, identifying oneself, and providing required assistance when a person or property is injured or damaged.

subsections.text: Leaving after a collision causing property damage without exchanging required information.
Leaving after a collision causing bodily injury without providing reasonable assistance.
Leaving a collision involving a fatality is an aggravated offense.

title: Driving Without a Valid License
description: Operating a motor vehicle on a public roadway without a valid license or while knowingly operating under a disqualifying suspension.

subsections.text: Operating without ever having obtained a valid license.
Operating while suspended or revoked.
Knowingly allowing an unlicensed person to operate a vehicle when the owner controls the vehicle.

title: Failure to Yield / Improper Right of Way
description: Failing to yield when required by traffic control devices, crossings, emergency operations, or established right-of-way rules.

subsections.text: Failing to yield at a stop sign, signal, or controlled intersection.
Failing to yield to a pedestrian lawfully occupying a marked crossing.
Failing to yield to an authorized emergency vehicle displaying required warning signals.

title: Eluding a Peace Officer
description: Willfully attempting to evade a marked peace officer in an identifiable police vehicle after a lawful signal to stop.

subsections.text: Failing to stop after emergency lights are activated and a lawful stop signal is given.
Continuing to flee after siren activation or repeated verbal commands.
Using dangerous speed, opposing traffic, or reckless maneuvers during the pursuit.

title: Forgery
description: Knowingly creating, altering, or using a false document, signature, credential, or record with intent to deceive or obtain a benefit.

subsections.text: Creating or altering a document to appear genuine.
Using a forged document while knowing it is false.
Forging an official government, court, license, or identification document is aggravating.

title: Fraud
description: Knowingly using deception, false representation, or concealment of a material fact to obtain money, property, services, or another benefit.

subsections.text: Obtaining property or services through a material false statement.
Using another person's identity or account information without authorization.
Conduct involving multiple victims or a coordinated scheme is aggravating.

title: Identity Theft
description: Knowingly obtaining, possessing, or using another person's identifying information without authorization for unlawful benefit or to facilitate an offense.

subsections.text: Using another person's name, identification number, credentials, or account information.
Possessing identifying information with intent to commit fraud.
Using stolen identity information to obtain government benefits, licenses, or official documents.

title: False Emergency Report
description: Knowingly making a false report to emergency services or law enforcement that causes or reasonably could cause a public safety response.

subsections.text: Reporting a nonexistent crime, fire, medical emergency, or dangerous event.
Providing knowingly false information that causes deployment of emergency personnel.
A false report causing substantial emergency resource diversion is aggravating.

title: Misuse of Emergency Communications
description: Knowingly using emergency radio channels, dispatch systems, or emergency hotlines for unauthorized or malicious purposes.

subsections.text: Transmitting non-emergency traffic on a restricted emergency channel after warning.
Impersonating dispatch or emergency personnel over an official communication system.
Interfering with active emergency traffic or dispatch instructions.

title: Interfering with a Peace Officer
description: Knowingly obstructing, delaying, distracting, or physically interfering with a peace officer performing lawful duties.

subsections.text: Physically preventing an officer from conducting a lawful arrest, search, or investigation.
Intentionally distracting or repeatedly interrupting an officer during active enforcement.
Driving or positioning a vehicle to block an officer performing official duties.

title: Tampering with Evidence
description: Knowingly destroying, altering, concealing, moving, or fabricating evidence with intent to impair its availability or integrity.

subsections.text: Destroying or discarding evidence after learning it may be relevant.
Moving or concealing evidence to prevent lawful recovery.
Fabricating evidence or planting an item to mislead investigators.

title: Criminal Conspiracy
description: Two or more persons knowingly agreeing to commit an offense and taking at least one substantial step toward the unlawful objective.

subsections.text: Entering an agreement to commit a felony.
Taking a substantial step demonstrating commitment to the agreed objective.
Recruiting, financing, supplying, or directing another participant may constitute a substantial step.

title: Accessory to a Felony
description: Knowingly assisting, facilitating, concealing, or profiting from a felony committed by another person without being the principal offender.

subsections.text: Providing transportation, tools, information, or resources with knowledge of the felony.
Helping the principal evade identification, arrest, or evidence recovery.
Receiving a benefit derived from the felony with knowledge of its criminal source.

title: Attempted Offense Modifier
description: A modifier applied when a person intentionally takes a substantial step toward an offense but the completed offense does not occur.

subsections.text: The person must possess intent to commit the underlying offense.
The conduct must move beyond mere preparation and constitute a substantial step.
The underlying eligible charge receives a 50 percent sentence reduction unless otherwise specified.

title: Crime Against a Government Employee Modifier
description: An aggravating modifier for an eligible offense committed against an on-duty peace officer, firefighter, paramedic, correctional officer, or designated government employee.

subsections.text: The victim is acting within official duties at the time of the offense.
The offender knew or reasonably should have known the victim's protected status.
The underlying sentence may be increased by 50 percent unless prohibited by the base charge.
